standard_prerequisites.name: Knuth equivalence for matchings
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two matchings are Knuth equivalent if they can be connected by the insertion and deletion moves of the section.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis is that the set is closed under this equivalence.

standard_prerequisites.name: Short statistic and unstable chords
standard_prerequisites.statement: Short is the statistic recording the positions of the short chords, and k denotes the number of unstable chords of a matching.
standard_prerequisites.use: The expansion is written in terms of s_{N-k,k} with k read off from any matching in the class.

standard_prerequisites.name: The transformation F
standard_prerequisites.statement: F(m) = (core(m), T(m)) is the bijection from matchings to pairs consisting of a core and a standard Young tableau, discussed in the retained subsection.
standard_prerequisites.use: Its restriction to a Knuth class is the statistic-preserving bijection at the heart of the proof.

core_obligations: Reduce to Knuth equivalence classes, since a disjoint union of Schur-positive sets is Schur-positive (source line 1224).

For a class M, use the retained characterisation of Knuth equivalence by the core to write M as the set of matchings with a fixed core m_0, with k and f determined by that core (source lines 1224-1225).
Restrict the transformation F to M and observe that it becomes a bijection onto {m_0} x Syt(N-k,k) that preserves the short statistic (source lines 1225-1228).
Apply the retained Schur-positivity criterion to conclude the two-row expansion with coefficient one (source line 1228).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce from arbitrary closed sets to equivalence classes.
Describe a class by its core using the characterisation theorem.
Restrict F to the class and apply the criterion.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled corollary `cor:closed under knuth like is schur positive` at source lines 1214-1221: a set of matchings closed under Knuth equivalence is Schur-positive for the short statistic, and a single Knuth class has generating function s_{N-k,k}. The proof (source lines 1223-1229) is short but it assembles three separate results: the reduction from a closed set to its equivalence classes by additivity of Schur-positivity (line 1224), the description of a class as all matchings with a fixed core obtained from the retained characterisation theorem (lines 1224-1225), and the restriction of the transformation F to that class, where it becomes a statistic-preserving bijection onto {m_0} x Syt(N-k,k) (lines 1226-1228). Only the final line invokes the Schur-positivity criterion, and the coefficient one comes from the bijection rather than from a computation.
